relevance_reason: Reports detailed phenotyping and IRF6 variants (Ile218Asn, Ser220Pro mosaic) in patients with IRF6-associated ectodermal dysplasia without clefting, the subject of ECTD19.

findings.statement: Schneider et al. (2026) described 2 unrelated male teenagers (P1, aged 17, and P2, aged 14) with ectodermal dysplasia who were born with natal teeth. P1 developed 7 deciduous teeth with delay and 12 permanent teeth (10 remaining), most with enamel defects and hypomineralization, and had a highly atrophic mandibular alveolar crest due to oligodontia; P2 developed only 9 permanent teeth. Both had overheating since infancy, anhidrosis with no sweat glands detectable on the palms, recurrent skin abscesses in the genital/gluteal area, behind the ears, axillae and mouth, very dry skin with plantar hyperkeratosis and blistering of the toes in winter, dysplastic thickened nails with distal onycholysis, thick nasal mucus, dry cerumen, and bilateral sensorineural hearing impairment since infancy; submucous cleft palate was excluded.
quotes: Patient 1 (P1) and patient 2 (P2), 17 and 14 years old, respectively, are unrelated male teenagers who had become noticeable already on their first day of life due to natal teeth

Investigations of the capability to perspire revealed anhidrosis, and no sweat glands were detectable on the palms by confocal laser scanning microscopy. Some toe‐ and fingernails were dysplastic, thickened or deformed with distal onycholysis.
Both subjects had a bilateral sensorineural hearing impairment since infancy, currently being treated with hearing aids. A submucous cleft palate was excluded in each case.

findings.statement: In P1 and P2, 2 unrelated males with ectodermal dysplasia with natal teeth, Schneider et al. (2026) identified the same de novo heterozygous c.653T>A transition in exon 6 of the IRF6 gene, resulting in an ile218-to-asn (I218N) substitution, by exome sequencing (P1) and Sanger sequencing (P2, after negative EDA, EDAR, EDARADD and TP63 testing). The variant was absent from parental DNA and was predicted to be deleterious.
quotes: Molecular genetic analysis of blood cells from these unrelated individuals revealed the same heterozygous substitution, c.653 T>A, chr1‐209 965 628 A>T, in exon 6 of the IRF6 gene, which led to an Ile218Asn exchange in the encoded protein predicted to be deleterious.
It was categorized as de novo, because the parents' DNA showed no alteration at this position.
Sanger sequencing of IRF6 was carried out after no pathogenic variants had been identified in the previous sequencing of EDA, EDAR, EDARADD and TP63.

findings.statement: Schneider et al. (2026) described a 22-year-old woman (P3) with anhidrosis, diffuse xerosis, dilated follicular ostia, heat intolerance, recurrent hidradenitis suppurativa-like abscesses of the groins, axillae and intergluteal fold, pincer nails of both great toes, bilateral acquired sensorineural hearing loss, epistaxis, crusted rhinitis, insufficient salivation, and bilateral superficial punctate keratitis with reduced tear film break-up time. Hair, lips, palate, breasts and nipples were normal and natal teeth were not remembered; she had 16 persisting deciduous teeth and only 2 permanent teeth after delayed eruption.
quotes: In patient 3 (P3), a 22‐year‐old woman referred for anhidrosis, dry skin and intolerance to environmental temperatures above 22°C, diffuse xerosis and dilatation of the follicular ostia were noted.
This patient also had pincer nails on both big toes. She showed no syndactyly and normal breasts and nipples. A bilateral acquired sensorineural hearing loss was diagnosed
Interestingly, patient 3 presented with 16 persisting deciduous teeth and only two permanent teeth after delayed tooth eruption.

findings.statement: In P3, Schneider et al. (2026) identified a de novo heterozygous c.658T>C transition in the IRF6 gene, resulting in a ser220-to-pro (S220P) substitution, by trio whole-genome sequencing; a variant allele frequency of 30.5% indicated mosaicism. In silico analyses supported pathogenicity, though the variant was formally classified as of unknown significance.
quotes: trio whole genome sequencing with a mean reading depth of 48× was performed and identified a heterozygous de novo IRF6 variant, c.658 T>C (p.Ser220Pro), with a variant allele frequency of 30.5% (T: 42 | C: 18) indicating mosaicism.

findings.statement: Comparing their 3 patients with 2 previously reported patients carrying IRF6 Ile218Asn or Ile218_Ser220delins variants, Schneider et al. (2026) considered oligodontia, hypo- or anhidrosis, hidradenitis suppurativa-like abscesses, poikiloderma, onychodysplasia and bilateral hearing impairment to be syndrome-defining (5/5), whereas natal teeth (2/5) and sparse hair (2/5) were irregular; none had lip pits, clefting, pterygia or syndactyly, distinguishing the disorder from VWS1 and PPS.
quotes: A combination of oligodontia, hypo‐ or anhidrosis, hidradenitis suppurativa‐like skin abscesses, poikiloderma, onychodysplasia and bilateral hearing impairment is considered to be syndrome‐defining, while natal teeth and sparse hair were observed irregularly or may be variable.

The absence of impaired palatal development in our patients or in the two additional patients described by others permits the conclusion that variants p.Ile218Asn, p.Ser220Pro and p.Ile218_Ser220delinsSerSerGlyAla do not limit the function and binding of the mutant protein to DNA

findings.statement: Schneider et al. (2026) recognized a common pattern of tooth agenesis in P1, P2 and P3: all had permanent upper incisors but no mandibular incisors or canines and no permanent premolars, with pronounced atrophy of the lower alveolar crest.
quotes: All three patients had permanent incisors in the upper jaw, but no incisors or canines in the mandible, and none of these unrelated individuals had any permanent premolars (Figure 4).

findings.statement: Schneider et al. (2026) found focal subcorneal clefting, basal spongiosis and absent sweat glands in skin biopsies from P1 and P3; keratinocyte nuclei of P1 showed stronger IRF6 immunostaining than controls, while P3 showed patchy nuclear staining consistent with mosaicism, and keratin 17 staining was normal. Together with genotype-phenotype data, they suggested a gain-of-function mechanism; AlphaFold3 modeling placed both substitutions in a short alpha-helix at the end of the region between the DNA-binding and protein-binding domains.
quotes: The nuclei of keratinocytes from P1 showed stronger specific staining (Figure 2E,F) than control nuclei (Figure 2A,B), while an apparently more patchy nuclear staining was observed in the epidermis of P3 (Figure 2G,H), fitting with genetic mosaicism. Sweat glands were absent in both patients.
Genotype-phenotype correlations from a total of five patients and immunohistochemical data support the assumption that IRF6-associated ED is based on a gain-of-function mechanism.
However, the point mutations causing the new disease entity both affect a short alpha‐helix at the end of this region, predicted with a considerably higher confidence value (mostly above 70).

findings.statement: Schneider et al. (2026) noted that they initially referred to this disorder as ectodermal dysplasia with natal teeth (EDNAT), but that natal teeth appeared less typical than initially thought.
quotes: We initially referred to this new disease as Ectodermal Dysplasia with Natal Teeth (EDNAT)
indicating that they are not as typical as initially thought.

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2026) reported that gain-of-function variants in the IRF6 gene cause a syndrome of hidradenitis suppurativa, ectodermal dysplasia, and deafness.
quotes: Gain-of-function variants in IRF6 cause hidradenitis suppurativa, ectodermal dysplasia and deafness syndrome.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It reports a new IRF6 variant that causes a new type of ectodermal dysplasia with natal teeth, which matches this entry's subject.

findings.statement: Peschel et al. (2025) reported a previously undescribed IRF6 variant that caused a new type of ectodermal dysplasia with natal teeth.
quotes: A yet undescribed IRF6 variant causes a new type of ectodermal dysplasia with natal teeth.
